In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the medical profession's institutional position is a crucial factor in explaining cross-country variation in the success of quality measurement.
the medical associations' institutional power is a key determinant of their ability to shape the quality measurement process.
the UK's success in introducing a system of surgical outcome measures is due, to a large degree, to the institutional position of the medical profession.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in a context where the medical association has a weak institutional position, government can successfully introduce a quality measurement system.
the more the state has been successful in establishing a strong institutional position for the medical profession, the more it has succeeded in implementing quality measures.
the medical profession in the UK was more willing to accept quality measures in the 2000's than it was in Israel in the 1990's.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a system where physicians are organized into a powerful professional association, the government is likely to encounter difficulties in implementing quality measurement reforms.
the medical profession's resistance to government's initiatives is not a universal phenomenon.
the medical profession's institutional position vis-a vis government is crucial in determining whether or not a quality measurement initiative is likely to succeed.
